domain_records.name: Callan-Harvey anomaly inflow on a finite slab lattice
domain_records.statement: Target: on a finite slab lattice the chiral variation of the boundary fermion determinant cancels the bulk Chern-Simons variation. Not established in this checkout. One tested candidate does not realize it, as expected: on open Wilson slabs with U(1) links, the gauge change acts on the Wilson matrix by a diagonal similarity, so the full, interior, boundary Schur and fixed site-matched chiral-block determinants are gauge invariant by construction, while a lifted cup-product CS term whose coefficient is not derived from the fermions changes by 1/32. This is a fixed-basis truncation of a vector-like regulator, not an obstruction to lattice inflow.
domain_records.obligation: Construct a regulated chiral boundary determinant whose projector, basis or measure depends on the gauge field (domain-wall or overlap/Ginsparg-Wilson type), derive from the same fermions the bulk Chern-Simons term they induce, and show that the two gauge variations cancel. The fixed-basis Wilson-slab test cannot register an anomaly, because site-matched fixed bases give similarity-invariant determinants; its bare lifted CS candidate is neither induced by the fermions nor well defined on U(1) links (an integer lift of the same links changes it by 1/8). The continuum Callan-Harvey mechanism remains a literature import.

domain_records.name: Does the obstruction a quantum computation generates limit its own ability to finish reliably
domain_records.statement: Every step of a noisy quantum computation, syndrome extraction and repair included, adds residual, and repair consumes capacity while adding residual of its own; the question is whether this makes reliable completion a self-referential no-go or a threshold condition that holds only under named resource assumptions (fresh supply, net-efficient repair, bounded overhead growth, physical error below threshold).
domain_records.obligation: The finite model answers the question as a threshold condition (QCV-Q1 to QCV-Q6); whether any physical system meets the named assumptions is not derived and no verdict on physical viability is given.
domain_records.audit: A question node: no Lean declaration states it; the derived records QCV-Q1 to QCV-Q6 carry the evidence.

domain_records.name: Finite model of per-step residual with repair that generates residual of its own
domain_records.statement: Backlog q(t+1) = max(0, q(t) + lam + g*mu - mu) in units of the Phi_1 repair cost, where lam is the residual generated per round by the computation, mu = kappa*r the repair rate from r fresh ancillas per round at kappa units each, and g the residual generated per unit of repair; with g = 0 this is the DS-QM101 queue; a distance-three level with a fault locations has constant c = a(a-1)/2.
domain_records.obligation: lam, g, kappa and r are declared inputs; no value is derived or measured for any code, and Phi_1 of a residual is not computed here.

declared self-generated fraction g of repair
declared capacity kappa per fresh ancilla

domain_records.name: Backlog is bounded exactly when the net repair rate covers generation; unit-gain repair never bounds it

domain_records.obligation: A statement inside the declared model; it does not say any code has g < 1 or that any supply r is available.
domain_records.audit: backlog_bounded_iff is an iff over the rationals with hypothesis 0 <= q0; the other three are direct corollaries stated with their own hypotheses. Axioms of the cited declarations: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound only.

domain_records.name: Concatenation recurrence p(k+1) = c*p(k)^2: exact closed form and threshold dichotomy over the rationals
domain_records.statement: For the recurrence p(k+1) = c*p(k)^2 over Q, c*p(k) = (c*p(0))^(2^k); for c > 0 and p(0) >= 0: if c*p(0) < 1 then p(k) tends to zero with c*p(k) <= (c*p(0))^(k+1) and, for c*p(0) <= 1/2, p(k) <= (1/2)^(2^k)/c; if c*p(0) = 1 then p(k) = 1/c for all k; if c*p(0) > 1 then p(k) diverges; so p(k) tends to zero iff p(0) < 1/c.
domain_records.obligation: The recurrence is the hypothesis; no noise model is shown to obey it and no constant c is computed for any code.
domain_records.audit: GoesToZero is the epsilon form over Q; Diverges means eventually above every bound; threshold_trichotomy states the three cases with the closed form in the first. Axioms of the cited declarations: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound only.

domain_records.name: Exact criterion on a level-dependent overhead for the existence of a threshold region
domain_records.statement: For p(k+1) = c(k)*p(k)^2 with c(k) >= 0, p(k) = p(0)^(2^k)*amp(k) with amp(0) = 1, amp(k+1) = c(k)*amp(k)^2, and some p(0) > 0 has p(k) tending to zero iff some M > 0 has amp(k) <= M^(2^k) for all k; the criterion holds for c(k) <= C, for c(k) <= A*B^(k+1) with A, B >= 1, for c(k) = (k+1)^2, and for c(k) <= a*b^N(k) with block size N(k+1) <= s*N(k), s < 2; it fails for c(k) >= a*b^(2^k) with a > 0, b > 1, and for c(k) >= a*b^N(k) with 2^k <= N(k), b > 1, where no positive p(0) has p(k) tending to zero.
domain_records.obligation: The families are exact illustrations of the criterion, not claims that any physical overhead has such a form; correlated-noise strength as an exponential of block size is a declared toy.

domain_records.name: Trace distance of two noisy unitary histories without fresh resources decays by the product of one minus the noise rates
domain_records.statement: For complex matrices of any size d and the variational trace norm tn(X) = sup over unitaries U of |tr(UX)|, the global depolarizing channel satisfies tn(Delta_p(rho) - Delta_p(sigma)) = (1-p)*tn(rho - sigma) for equal-trace rho, sigma and p <= 1; along any history of unitaries V(i) with depolarizing rates p(i) in [0,1], tn(run rho - run sigma) = (product of (1-p(i)))*tn(rho - sigma), which is at most (1-p)^t*tn(rho - sigma) when every p(i) >= p, and (1-p)^t <= 1/(1+p*t).
domain_records.obligation: The trace norm is the variational form, whose equality with the sum of singular values is cited; the noise is global depolarizing with a declared rate per step, not independent per-qubit noise, and the statement is about histories without fresh resets.

domain_records.statement: For rational Bloch vectors, noisy steps r -> (1-p)*R*r with rational rotations R (R^T R = 1) give sqDist(run r, run s) = (product of (1-p(i))^2)*sqDist(r, s), at most ((1-p)^2)^t*sqDist(r, s) when every p(i) in [p,1]; and (v.sigma)^2 = (v.v)*1 over the complex numbers, so the difference of two qubit states has both singular values |r-s|/2.
